speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a child experiencing frequent nosebleeds, bleeding from your mouth, and tiny red spots on your skin. To understand the cause, how long have these symptoms been happening, and do you have a history of bruising easily?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given the child's age and the combination of frequent epistaxis, gum bleeding, and petechiae on the extremities, have there been any episodes of excessive bleeding after minor injuries or surgeries?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Frequent epistaxis. I also have Mucous membrane bleeding, Diffuse petechiae on distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Idiopathic Thrombocytopenic Purpura (ITP).

The clinical picture of mucosal bleeding, petechiae on the distal extremities, and easy bruising in a 4-year-old is classic for ITP. I will proceed with requesting a Complete Blood Count (CBC) to confirm the platelet count and rule out other causes. REQUEST TEST: CBC
